trans-unit.source: Bloom failed to update from version {0} to version {1}. If this continues to happen, try restarting your computer. If it still happens, please Report a Problem.
trans-unit.note: ID: CollectionTab.VelopackUpdateFailed

Shown as a toast when Bloom detects that a background update failed to install (e.g., a running process prevented it). {0} is the version Bloom was running before the update, {1} is the version it tried to update to.
This isn't used by code, but rather we harvest some of these for use in making the GIF that shows when the software is installing.
In English, given the context, just "Installing..." is enough. But your translation can be verbose, like "Software Installation in Progress...".

Second paragraph of a message whose first line is "This program cannot write to the folder {0}." (Errors.DefenderFolderProtectionHeading), shown soon after a collection opens when Bloom finds that Windows won't let it create, change, rename or delete some kinds of files in the collection's folder. It is followed by Errors.FolderAntivirusProtection or Errors.FolderNotWritable.

trans-unit.source: Antivirus software, such as Avast's Ransomware Shield or Windows Security's Controlled Folder Access, may be stopping Bloom. Tell that program that you trust Bloom.
trans-unit.note: ID: Errors.FolderAntivirusProtection

Part of a message whose first line is "This program cannot write to the folder {0}." (Errors.DefenderFolderProtectionHeading), shown when Bloom can't write in a folder it needs and antivirus may be the cause; it is followed by a link to a help page. "Ransomware Shield" is the name of a feature of the Avast antivirus program, and "Controlled Folder Access" is the name of a setting in Windows Security; use the names those programs show in your language, if they are translated.

trans-unit.source: You may not have permission to change files there, or the folder may be read-only. Choose a folder you can change, or ask whoever manages this computer or network for permission.
trans-unit.note: ID: Errors.FolderNotWritable

Part of a message whose first line is "This program cannot write to the folder {0}." (Errors.DefenderFolderProtectionHeading), shown when Bloom can't write in a folder it needs because the user lacks permission or the folder is read-only; it is followed by a link to a help page.
